**How do I vote absentee in South Carolina?**

You can vote absentee in South Carolina by mail or in person.

**To vote absentee by mail:**

1. You must request an absentee ballot. You can do this online at scVOTES.gov, by mail, or in person at your county voter registration office.
2. Once you have requested an absentee ballot, you will receive it in the mail.
3. Fill out the ballot and return it to your county voter registration office by mail or in person.

**To vote absentee in person:**

1. You must go to your county voter registration office during early voting or on Election Day.
2. Bring your photo ID and proof of residency.
3. You will be given an absentee ballot to fill out and cast.

**Where can I vote in South Carolina?**

You can vote at the polling place in your precinct. You can find your polling place by visiting scVOTES.gov and selecting “Find My Polling Place” under MySCVotes or by checking with your county voter registration office.

**What hours are polling places open on Election Day?**

Polling places will be open 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. As long as you are in line by 7:00 p.m., you will be allowed to vote.

**What do I take with me to vote?**

You must bring a photo ID with you to vote. You can also bring proof of residency, but this is not required.

**What if I have questions about voting in South Carolina?**

You can contact your county voter registration office for help with voting in South Carolina. You can also find more information on the South Carolina Election Commission website.

column8: Who can vote absentee?
column12:
State law allows voters with qualifying reasons to vote absentee by mail:

Persons with employment obligations which prevent them from voting during early voting hours for the duration of the early voting period, and during the hours the polls are open on election day.
Persons attending a sick or physically disabled person which prevents them from voting during early voting hours for the duration of the early voting period, and during the hours the polls are open on election day.
Persons confined to a jail or pretrial facility pending disposition of arrest or trial which prevents them from voting during early voting hours for the duration of the early voting period, and during the hours the polls are open on election day.
Persons who will be absent from their county of residence during early voting hours for the duration of the early voting period, and during the hours the polls are open on election day.
Persons with physical disabilities.
Persons sixty-five years of age or older.
Members of the Armed Forces and Merchant Marines of the United States, their spouses, and dependents residing with them (Learn more about procedures related to Military and Overseas Citizens).
Persons admitted to a hospital as an emergency patient on the day of the election or within a four-day period before the election (see additional details below).
column13:
In South Carolina, you can vote absentee if you meet one of the following criteria:

* You will be absent from your county of residence on Election Day and during the early voting period.
* You are confined to your home due to illness or physical disability.
* You are the parent or guardian of a child who is confined to their home due to illness or physical disability.
* You are a religious observer whose religious tenets forbid secular (non-religious) activity on Election Day.
* You are a student who is attending school outside of your county of residence.
* You are a member of the military or other uniformed service who is stationed outside of your county of residence.
* You are an overseas voter.

You can request an absentee ballot by mail or in person at your county voter registration office. The deadline to request an absentee ballot varies depending on the election, so be sure to check with your county voter registration office for more information.

Here are some additional things to keep in mind about absentee voting in South Carolina:

* You must be a registered voter in order to vote absentee.
* You must sign your absentee ballot application and ballot.
* You must return your absentee ballot by the deadline specified on the ballot application.

Return your ballot to your county voter registration office or an early voting center either by mail or personal delivery.

Driver’s license issued by a state within the United States.
Another form of identification containing a photograph issued by the Department of Motor Vehicles or its equivalent by a state within the United States.
Passport.
Military identification containing a photograph issued by the federal government.
South Carolina voter registration card containing a photograph of the voter.
Place the ballot in the “ballot here-in” envelope and place the “ballot here-in” envelope in the return envelope.

Hi Harry! Here are the things you need to bring with you to vote in South Carolina:

* **A photo ID:** This is required for all voters in South Carolina. Acceptable forms of ID include:
    * A driver's license issued by South Carolina or another state.
    * A state ID card issued by South Carolina or another state.
    * A passport.
    * A military ID.
    * A voter registration card with a photo.
* **Your voter registration card:** This is not required, but it can be helpful to have with you.
* **A sample ballot:** This is not required, but it can be helpful to have with you so you know what races and measures are on the ballot.

If you do not have a photo ID, you can still vote by bringing two forms of non-photo ID that show your name and address. Acceptable forms of non-photo ID include:

* A utility bill.
* A bank statement.
* A paycheck.
* A government document.

You can also vote without ID if you sign an affidavit stating that you are who you say you are and that you do not have a photo ID.

column12:
Make your voting experience as fast and easy as possible by getting a free Photo ID before voting.

If you are already registered to vote, you can go to your county elections office to get a SC Voter Registration Card with Photo.  You will need to provide your date of birth and the last four digits of your Social Security Number.  You can do this even on Election Day.  Free DMV ID Cards are also available from the Department of Motor Vehicles.

If you cannot get a Photo ID, bring your non-photo voter registration card with you when leaving to vote.

You may vote a provisional ballot after signing an affidavit stating you have a reasonable impediment to obtaining a Photo ID.  A reasonable impediment is any valid reason, beyond your control, which created an obstacle to obtaining a Photo ID.  Some examples include:  a disability or illness, a conflict with your work schedule, a lack of transportation, a lack of a birth certificate, family responsibilities, a religious objection to being photographed, and any other obstacle you find reasonable.

This ballot will count unless someone proves to the county board of voter registration and elections that you are lying about your identity or having the listed impediment.
